memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: COPD (GOLD 2) and episodic migraine.
Patient reports dyspnea on exertion, occasional wheeze, and migraine headaches twice weekly. On exam: mild pursed-lip breathing, bilateral wheezes, normal neurological exam. Spirometry shows FEV1 1.8 L (55% predicted), FVC 2.2 L, FEV1/FVC 0.82. ACT score 16 (not well controlled). Inhaler technique checked: incorrect; taught correct use of budesonide-formoterol dry powder device, inspiratory flow adequate. Smoking status: former, stopped 2010, 10 pack-years.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Tiotropium inhaler OD; Salbutamol inhaler SOS; Budesonide-formoterol 200/6 inhaler BD; Propranolol 40 mg OD; Sumatriptan 50 mg SOS; Topiramate 25 mg HS; Naproxen 500 mg SOS. Duration 3 months.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Hemoglobin 13.2 g/dl (12-16); WBC 6.8 x10^9/L (4-10); Platelets 210 x10^9/L (150-400); ESR 12 mm/hr (<20); CRP 2 mg/L (<5).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Chest X-ray: hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation, cardiac size normal.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been using my inhalers as prescribed, but I still get shortness of breath when climbing stairs and my migraines have worsened to three times a week despite sumatriptan.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Budesonide-formoterol 400/12 inhaler BD; Tiotropium inhaler OD; Salbutamol inhaler SOS; Propranolol 60 mg OD; Topiramate 50 mg HS; Sumatriptan 50 mg SOS; Naproxen 500 mg SOS. Duration 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: COPD (GOLD 2) and episodic migraine, stable on therapy.
Patient reports improved exertional dyspnea, now only on steep slopes; migraines reduced to twice weekly. Exam: mild wheeze at bases, otherwise clear lungs; no neurological deficits. Spirometry: FEV1 1.9 L (58% predicted), FVC 2.3 L, FEV1/FVC 0.83; change in FEV1 since last test +0.1 L. ACT score 20 (well controlled). Inhaler technique checked: correct; inspiratory flow adequate for dry powder device. Smoking status: former, stopped 2010, 10 pack-years.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Spirometry: FEV1 1.9 L (58% predicted), FVC 2.3 L, FEV1/FVC 0.83; FVC 2.3 L (80% predicted).

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow-up appointment booked with Dr Suresh Menon (D05) for 2025-10-05 at 10:00 AM.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Referral to Neurology for refractory migraine prophylaxis. Patient experiencing migraines twice weekly despite current prophylaxis; consider specialist input for alternative agents.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Neurology review: recommended continuing propranolol 60 mg OD, add amitriptyline 10 mg HS, maintain sumatriptan SOS. No urgent intervention required.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: COPD (GOLD 2) and episodic migraine, well controlled.
Patient denies dyspnea at rest, reports only mild breathlessness on brisk walking; migraines now once weekly. Exam: clear lungs, no wheeze; normal neurological exam. Spirometry: FEV1 2.0 L (60% predicted), FVC 2.4 L, FEV1/FVC 0.83; change in FEV1 since last test +0.1 L. ACT score 22 (well controlled). Inhaler technique checked: correct; inspiratory flow adequate. Smoking status: former, stopped 2010, 10 pack-years.
